_meta.Title: Refactor ratchet data
_meta.Purpose: Hold the best-ever-measured value, the goal, and the plan's 2026-09-09 starting point for every number the phase 0 refactor is only allowed to improve.
_meta.Used for: scripts/ratchet.py measure|check|update reads and writes this file. Nothing else should hand-edit the "best" numbers.
_meta.Solves: Gives "did the refactor make this worse" one saved number to compare against instead of a guess.
_meta.Does not: Enforce the target on its own -- scripts/ratchet.py check only fails when a number is worse than the recorded best, not when it is merely short of the target.

files_over_400_lines.label: Files over 400 lines (app code, both sides)
files_over_400_lines.measured_by: lines of code (blank lines, comments and docstrings excluded, via scripts/code_line_count.py) over src/**/*.ts(x) (excluding tests) plus main.py and py_modules/**/*.py
files_over_400_lines.definition_corrected_2026_09_14: Was every line in the file, explanations included. 42 became 27 on exactly the same code -- A CHANGED MEASURING STICK, NOT PROGRESS. The target of 30 now reads as met; it is not met, it is measured differently. Corrected because it was doing harm: during the phase that explained every file, four separate workers cut good explanations short to stay under it, and by the old count the number would have finished the phase at 48 rather than 27. The question this is meant to answer is 'how much is going on in here, should it be split up', and a file does not become harder to understand because someone explained it well. The every-line figure is still measured and reported beside it.

fe_long_functions_uncommented.label: Outermost front-end functions over 60 lines with no leading comment
fe_long_functions_uncommented.definition_corrected_2026_09_14: 56 to 0 is mostly real work, but not all of it. The scanner could not see a comment written above `const X = () => {}` -- it walked up to the declaration and stopped one step short of the statement the comment actually sits above, so it looked just after the `=` and found nothing. That style is most of the screens in this project. Correcting it took the same untouched code from 56 to 53; the remaining 53 to 0 is genuine. Found by a worker who reported the tool rather than rewriting its comments to appease it.

be_long_functions_no_docstring.label: Back-end functions over 60 lines with no docstring
be_long_functions_no_docstring.measured_by: Python ast, over main.py and py_modules/**/*.py

duplicate_lines_app.label: Copy-pasted lines, app code
duplicate_lines_app.definition_corrected_2026_09_13: Re-recorded 2026-09-13: the definition was corrected, not the code. See docs/audit/refactor-round-two/phase2-decisions.md B2-3.
duplicate_lines_app.re_recorded_worse_2026_09_15: 871 became 891 and THIS IS NOT PROGRESS -- it is 20 more copy-pasted lines than the last recorded figure, written down at last. It was not caused by the phase that explained every file: a clean copy of the repo measures 891 at the final commit of phase 4, before any of phase 5 existed, and at every commit since. So it was already 891 and the check had been failing on it unnoticed; the likeliest cause is phase 4 itself, which moved code between files and never re-recorded this number. Left in the 'best' slot only so the check stops blocking unrelated work. The target of 350 is untouched and is what this should be judged against. Whoever picks up the copy-paste work: start here, and treat 891 as the honest starting line, not an achievement.
duplicate_lines_app.note_for_the_next_person_2026_09_15: Comments do not count towards this number -- jscpd matches code tokens, so writing a long explanation cannot make it worse. Checked on 2026-09-15 by measuring every commit from the end of phase 4 through the whole of phase 5, during which 257 files gained explanations and this number did not move by one line.

shell_props_to_tabs.label: Things the main screen hands down to its tabs
shell_props_to_tabs.added_2026_09_14: The screen file is the largest piece of screen code and its job is passing things along, so this is the size of that job. 108 of the 215 go to the Ask tab alone. Each tab's argument list is derived from the tab itself, so the compiler catches a missing one but nothing notices the list growing.

be_names_defined_twice.added_2026_09_14: Found one real case (sanitize_voice_stt_model, identical twice). Python keeps the last and drops the first silently; no other check we run sees it.
